text:
alice_support: FYI — customer AcmeRetail on Dedicated reported a spike of 429s and occasional AUTH_FAILUREs after last night's maintenance window. They say autoscaling didn't bring up nodes quick enough (min_replicas=2, max_replicas=40). Issue started ~03:40 UTC and lasted ~20m.

alice_support: Quick stats from them: traffic ~6x baseline, queued_requests peaked at ~180, avg response_time spiked to 2.3s then 5-6s, many 429s. They provided these logs:
```
2026-11-02T03:41:12Z ERROR request_id=acme-req-23 status=429 reason="quota_exceeded"
2026-11-02T03:41:13Z WARN auth token=redacted module="token_verify" error="token_verify_failed" retry=1
metric.queued_requests=180 metric.backlog_ms=5200
```

alice_support: They can reproduce with a simple load script. Repro steps attached by customer: use their dedicated endpoint + API key and run 500 rps for 3 min.

ben_engineer: Can you paste the dedicated pool id and customer org id? Also, do we have autoscaler controller logs for that timeframe?

alice_support: org=acme-retail pool=ded-prod-eu-7. I'll attach their load script, token (sensitive) to the ticket.

carla_platform: Checking controller logs now. Early snippet shows scaling attempts were queued:
```
[2026-11-02T03:40:55Z] autoscaler: desired_replicas=18 current_replicas=2 reason="latency_slo_breach"
[2026-11-02T03:41:00Z] autoscaler: scale_op enqueued id=op-842 rate_limit=1/min
[2026-11-02T03:41:00Z] autoscaler: maintenance_mode=false but scale_ops_rate_limit=1
[2026-11-02T03:42:05Z] provisioner: provisioning_request id=pr-551 status=pending
[2026-11-02T03:44:10Z] provisioner: provisioning_request id=pr-551 status=failed reason="az_quota_exceeded"
```

carla_platform: Looks like our autoscaler rate_limit combined with a provisioning failure (AZ quota) prevented us from reaching desired replicas quickly. Rate limit is currently set to 1 scale op/min for that cluster.

ben_engineer: Oof. Two contributors then: (1) rate limit too conservative for sudden 6x spikes, (2) infra quota blocking provisioning. Does provisioner retry?

dan_infra: Provisioner does retry but backoff is exponential and cloud quota errors can take minutes if quota needs request approval. I see elevated provisioning latency in eu-west-1 last night. There's also a temporary soft quota reduce applied for that account during maintenance.

eva_cs: Customer is on call with SE now, they're pretty upset. They said tokens started failing (AUTH_FAILURE) intermittently while requests were queued. Could be a side-effect of high queue/backpressure leading to timeouts in our auth middleware.

fred_billing: Quick note — I saw a billing webhook failure for AcmeRetail at 03:38 UTC (payment retry). Not sure it caused token invalidation, but flagging in case their billing state toggled something on our side (suspended tokens). I'll cross-check.

oncall-bot: [Alert] dedicated_pool.ded-prod-eu-7 high_queue_length=180 > alert_threshold(100) at 2026-11-02T03:41:20Z. Incident created: INC-20261102-72.

ben_engineer: Proposed immediate remediation steps we can try now: 1) temporarily bump min_replicas to 8 for ded-prod-eu-7 (manual override), 2) trigger manual scale out (create scale_op bypassing rate limit), 3) request emergency quota bump in cloud console, 4) roll back any maintenance-mode flags. Any objections?

carla_platform: I'm OK with manual scale and bypassing rate limit for the pool while infra works on quota. We should capture why rate_limit=1 exists (safety) and add a burst path for verified emergencies.

dan_infra: Requesting quota bump now (case 0123456). Also increasing provisioner retry aggressiveness temporarily for that pool.

fred_billing: Confirmed billing webhook retried and payment cleared at 03:46 UTC. No token-suspend action taken by billing subsystem, so AUTH_FAILUREs likely from our auth timeout under load, not payment.

alice_support: I'll tell customer we're doing a manual scale and quota request. They're asking for repro steps so SE can verify. Their script is:
```
# reproduce (customer):
for i in {1..500}; do
  hey -c 50 -q 500 -z 3m -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://dedicated.acme-retail.redwood.ai/v1/generate
done
```

ben_engineer: After manual scale we should watch queued_requests, auth error rate, and token verify latency. Also collect kube node bootstrap logs to see why nodes failed to join quickly.

carla_platform: Manual actions done: min_replicas set 8 at 03:43:10Z, manual scale op invoked bypassing rate limit; cloud provisioner started new instances at 03:43:25Z.

oncall-bot: [Info] manual_scale executed by carla_platform for pool=ded-prod-eu-7 new_replicas=8 at 2026-11-02T03:43:25Z.

alice_support: Customer reports 429s dropping dramatically within ~3 minutes after the manual scale. They still saw a few AUTH_FAILUREs but far fewer.

dan_infra: Quota bump approved at 03:47, provisioner retried and new instances reached Ready at 03:49:00Z. Kube join logs show a transient CNI timeout during bootstrap — likely due to AZ networking degradation.

eva_cs: Customer confirmed service recovered at 03:50 UTC and will file a postmortem request. They're asking for an explanation and a preventative plan.

ben_engineer: Action items: (1) add an emergency-burst path to autoscaler to allow N immediate ops when SLO-wide breach detected, (2) add a gating check that surfaces AZ quota or provisioning failures to ops earlier, (3) investigate auth middleware timeouts under long queue/backpressure and add circuit breaker for token verification. I'll create tickets.

carla_platform: I'll own rollout of a temporary autoscaler policy change that allows higher ephemeral scale rate for TrustedEnterprise pools.

dan_infra: I'll follow up on CNI/AZ networking incident with cloud vendor and ensure quota alerting is improved.

fred_billing: I'll confirm there are no billing side-effects and update AcmeRetail billing contact.

alice_support: Thanks everyone. Marking thread resolved for now; customer is happy with workaround but wants the postmortem and mitigation plan.

oncall-bot: [Resolve] Incident INC-20261102-72 resolved at 2026-11-02T03:50:10Z.
